The Official Government Documents Register

A source-linked catalogue of government records, administrative correspondence, legal documents, official determinations and other documentary evidence preserved in The Witness Remains archive.

The Witness Remains — Dr Barran Dodger documentary archive. Dr Richard William McLean, publicly known as Dr Barran Dodger.

Back to the main archive

Scope

This is a documentary finding aid. It is not a court, a tribunal, an official investigation, or a determination of liability. Inclusion of a document does not establish wrongdoing, motive, unlawful conduct, or personal responsibility.

The first review looked at the public repository wezzo72/Barrandodger at commit 1b98e6efea73f2633ac089cba0594cf968fd7cac on 11 October 2026. That tree contained 6,617 files, including 3,647 PDFs, and produced entries OGDR-001 to OGDR-125.

A further pass the same day re-counted the tree at commit 7c9c609d8da2: 6,706 files, including 3,650 PDFs. Every PDF path was screened. 418 PDFs that were not already registered, and whose folder or filename indicated government administration or correspondence, were downloaded and had their opening pages read. 60 of those were byte-identical to an entry already in the register. 270 distinct further records are entered in section 13. Website-backup renders, generated page PDFs, AI essays, gospels, prophecy, and files whose names did not indicate a government record were not opened and are not treated as government findings.

What the first pass covered. Files in docs/official-drive/, the text-extracted copies used to read them, and selected files in imports/official-2026-10-01/. Where two files had the same SHA-256, they are one entry.

What the further pass covered. Curated official shelves (docs/email-extracts/, docs/official-gmail/, docs/drive-evidence/, official-import folders, and the government shelf of the Gmail sweep), plus other PDFs whose filenames named an agency, a tribunal, a decision, a notice, or FOI correspondence. Opening pages only, up to three pages. Archive placeholders that say they are not the document were not registered as the document.

What was still not opened. The barrandodger.com website backup, rendered-pdfs/, AI essays, gospels, prophecy, and the large remainder of the 3,650 PDFs whose paths did not indicate a government record. They remain in the repository for inspection. Several scans returned no text layer. Encrypted PDFs were not decrypted.

Last review: 11 October 2026. Preservation first. Verification second. Context third. Conclusions last.

Methodology and evidence scale

Official records are the primary source for factual statements in this register. The author’s later letters and archive covers are identified as such. A filename is not a finding. A Git blob SHA is a version-control identifier, not a SHA-256 hash. SHA-256 values below were computed in this review from the bytes downloaded from GitHub. No blockchain timestamp was re-checked for this register.

  • A — Directly established documentary fact, limited to what the inspected pages say.
  • B — Corroborated claim supported by more than one identifiable record.
  • C — Documented allegation or reported experience, not independently established.
  • D — Reasoned inference requiring further verification.
  • E — Speculation or unresolved interpretation. This register avoids E.

The classification attaches to the proposition in the entry, not automatically to every sentence in the file.

Records that particularly matter

These are not the whole register. They are the records, among those opened, that most directly show an official acknowledgement, a decision about employment, disability support, money, legal status or access, or a refusal, review or jurisdictional limit. The selection is explained in each entry. Unresolved questions are stated as questions.

27 March 2023, Scott Tredwell. The file is a three-page letter from the Federal Court Principal Registry, signed Scott Tredwell, General Counsel. He writes as an authorised officer under the Public Interest Disclosure Act 2013 (Cth). It is not a judgment.

On the information provided to him, he says he is satisfied Dr McLean is or was an employee of the Department of Social Services under the trading name Rich McLean, Arts Life Coach, Peer-Support Worker & Mental Health Advocate. In the same letter he is not satisfied the disclosure was made by a public official or to an authorised recipient, he finds the conduct does not relate to the Federal Court, the Federal Circuit and Family Court, or the National Native Title Tribunal, and he decides not to allocate the disclosure. He assumes, for the initial assessment only, that the conduct described is disclosable conduct. That assumption is not a finding that the conduct occurred.

A different statute and a different decision-maker are involved in the Administrative Appeals Tribunal decision of 12 July 2023, which affirmed Comcare’s decision and, in the catchwords, held that the applicant was not an employee of the Commonwealth for the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 1988 (Cth). Those two records are not interchangeable.

Official status and provenance
Not a court finding. The signatory is not established from the extract. Later AAT affirmation is a separate document.
Substantive contents
Addressed to Dr Richard William McLean, 2 McCubbin Street, Footscray. States the claim for workers’ compensation is declined under s 14 of the SRC Act for anxiety state and depressive disorder. Claimed condition: anxiety and depression. The reasons begin with whether the person is an “employee” under s 5. The letter records that the claim form of 26 April 2021 described the usual occupation as artist–life coach–therapeutic supplier and sole trader, and that a 13 May 2021 email said he was a registered NDIA provider, an employer of himself, paid through PRODA. The extracted pages discuss indicia of a contract of service. The final operative sentence of the employment analysis was not fully captured beyond the opening reasons. The letter attaches a notice of rights and says a reconsideration may be requested within 30 days.
Significance
It is the primary compensation refusal later taken to the AAT.
Potential detriment or consequences
The claim is declined. The letter does not state a dollar amount of compensation refused.
Causal qualification
Expressly recorded: the claim is declined. Downstream loss of income is the author’s characterisation unless another record quantifies it. Not established as a dollar figure here.
Corroborating records
AAT decision 12 July 2023; NDIS Commission email of 3 June 2021 about provider status.
Evidence classification
A for the decline and the employment question as framed in the letter. The full reasoning after the pages extracted is not fully established by this entry.
Verification status
Inspected 11 October 2026. 3 pages extracted.

Official status and provenance
Not a finding that Dr McLean was or was not an employee of the NDIA or of the Department of Social Services. Not a decision under the SRC Act or the PID Act.
Substantive contents
The email says NDIS providers are their own business, that registration audits do not make the recipient an employee of the NDIS Commission, and that an enquiry about employment status with the NDIA should go to enquiries@ndis.gov.au.
Significance
It is an official email distinguishing registered-provider status from employment by the Commission. It is often relevant to how later employment arguments are framed. It does not decide them.
Potential detriment or consequences
No financial amount or service withdrawal is recorded in the email.
Causal qualification
No causal finding. The email gives a direction about where to ask an employment question.
Corroborating records
Comcare determination 26 May 2021; AAT decision 12 July 2023; Tredwell letter 27 March 2023.
Evidence classification
A for the email’s statements. Any use of the email as proof of NDIA employment or non-employment is D at most and is not adopted here.

Official status and provenance
This is not a court judgment, a judicial finding, or a determination of liability. The sentence about Department of Social Services employment is expressly “on the information you have provided me.” It is not an independent employment investigation and it is not a finding under the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 1988 (Cth). The later sentence that he is not satisfied the disclosure “was made by a public official or provided to an authorised recipient” sits in the same letter. The two statements are not the same legal conclusion and are not collapsed here. The assumption that conduct is disclosable is made for the initial assessment. It is not a finding that the conduct occurred. A second file, “2023 03 27 Final Assessment - Dr Rich McLean 86.pdf”, has a different SHA-256 but the same letter wording on the pages read. It is a second copy, not a second decision.
Substantive contents
Three-page letter on Federal Court Principal Registry letterhead, Harry Gibbs Commonwealth Law Courts, Brisbane, addressed to Dr Rich McLean at richarddrawstuff@gmail.com. Tredwell states he is an officer engaged under the Public Service Act 1999 (Cth), authorised by the Court’s Chief Executive Officer and Principal Registrar to carry out authorised-officer functions under the PID Act. He records that on 7 March 2023 an email to Sia Lagos asked that struggles, oppression, victimisation and detriments “in psychological, financial, reputation and other ways” be acknowledged and compensated. On the information provided to him, he writes: “I am satisfied that you are, or were, an employee with the Department of Social Services, providing services under the trading name Rich McLean, Arts Life Coach, Peer-Support Worker & Mental Health Advocate.” He also writes that he is satisfied the conduct disclosed “does not relate in any way to the Federal Court, FCFCOA or the NNTT,” and that he is not satisfied the disclosure was provided to an authorised recipient. He is satisfied that Dr McLean believes the information tends to show conduct within PID Act s 29 items concerning perverting the course of justice, maladministration, and danger to health or safety, and says it is difficult to determine whether that belief is on reasonable grounds. For the initial assessment he is “prepared to assume” the conduct is disclosable conduct. The decision paragraph states he is not satisfied the disclosure “was made by a public official or provided to an authorised recipient,” so there is no reasonable basis to decide it is an internal disclosure (s 43(2)), and he decides not to allocate it. No further PID Act action will be taken by the Federal Court or FCFCOA on that material. Other agencies’ own PID matters are expressly unaffected. The letter is signed “Scott Tredwell, General Counsel.”
Significance
It is a direct official assessment of whether material sent to the Federal Court would be allocated under the PID Act, and it is the record that discusses the Department of Social Services employment question in the author’s later correspondence. It matters because later argument treats it as confirmation of employment or of protected-disclosure status. The letter itself does not allocate a disclosure and does not decide a compensation claim.
Potential detriment or consequences
The letter records the author’s request that psychological, financial, reputation and other detriments be acknowledged and compensated. That is the author’s reported experience, as summarised by the officer. The decision not to allocate means the Federal Court and FCFCOA will take no further PID Act action on this disclosure. Any broader financial, service or employment consequence is not established by this letter alone.
Causal qualification
Expressly recorded: no further PID Act action by the Federal Court or FCFCOA on this disclosure. The author’s account of detriment is recorded as what he asked to have acknowledged. A causal claim that the non-allocation itself produced a later loss of income, support or employment is not established by this letter.
Corroborating records
Second scan: 2023 03 27 Final Assessment - Dr Rich McLean 86.pdf (different hash, same wording on pages read). Later party letter: 08.01.2024 scott treadwell Federal Court - superannuation and NDIS CEO copy 2.pdf. Distinct statutory question: AAT decision 12 July 2023, McLean and Comcare, file 2021/7478.
Evidence classification
A for the wording of the letter on the pages read. The DSS employment sentence is A as a statement the letter makes, and is qualified by the letter’s own words “on the information you have provided me.” It is not A as an independent finding of a contract of employment. Claims that the letter is a court judgment, or that it establishes SRC Act employment, are not supported (not A).
Verification status
Inspected 11 October 2026. Text extracted from all 3 pages. SHA-256 computed from the downloaded file. Link checked as a GitHub blob URL at commit 1b98e6ef.

Official status and provenance
Grant of access to five departmental documents is not a finding about their contents. Those contents were not read as part of this entry. The schedule was not fully text-extracted. This does not establish what every other agency holds.
Substantive contents
The letter records the original refusal notification of 14 April 2022 under s 24A(1)(b). It records that on 11 April 2023 the Department told the OAIC it had found some material that might relate to the applicant but was not satisfied of a positive match. On 15 August 2024 the OAIC provided residential addresses in New South Wales (2009) and Victoria (2012). The revised decision: the Department holds five documents that meet the request; access is granted in full, with irrelevant material deleted under s 22(1)(a)(ii), including non-SES contact details, signatures, and parts that do not relate to the applicant, including extracts of media reports about other topics. A revised decision does not automatically end the IC review.
Significance
It changes the earlier “documents do not exist” refusal and identifies five departmental documents as within scope.
Potential detriment or consequences
The original refusal delayed access. The revised decision grants access with deletions. No further detriment is calculated.
Causal qualification
The change of decision is expressly tied to additional identifying information from the OAIC. Other consequences are not established.
Corroborating records
FOI-2022-045-Decision.pdf. A documents-release PDF exists (FOI-2022-045IC-Documents-for-release.pdf) and was not text-inspected because of size.
Evidence classification
A for the revised decision as stated.
Verification status
Inspected 11 October 2026. 3 pages.

Official status and provenance
This is a tribunal decision, not a Federal Court judgment. It does not decide the PID Act allocation question in the 27 March 2023 Tredwell letter. The employment test recorded in the catchwords is the SRC Act test. It is not the same sentence as Tredwell’s statement, made on information provided to him, that Dr McLean was or had been a Department of Social Services employee for PID Act purposes. The full reasoning beyond the opening pages was not line-read in this review.
Substantive contents
The first page states: “The Tribunal affirms the decision the subject of review,” signed Senior Member C. J. Furnell, 12 July 2023, Melbourne, file 2021/7478, Re Richard McLean and Comcare. The catchwords, on the pages read, describe a compensation claim for psychological injury (depression and anxiety state) under the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 1988 (Cth), and state that it was held the applicant was not an employee of the Commonwealth, a Commonwealth authority, or a corporation licensed under that Act as a self-insurer, where the applicant was a registered NDIS provider, and that the reviewable decision was affirmed. Only the opening pages were read in full for this entry. The reasons continue for 21 pages.
Significance
It is a formal decision on the compensation claim Comcare had declined, and it is the clearest official record in this set on the SRC Act employment question. It sits beside, and does not erase, the different PID Act letter of 27 March 2023.
Potential detriment or consequences
The operative result on page 1 is that the decision under review was affirmed, so the compensation decision was not changed. Financial consequences of that affirmation are not calculated in the pages read.
Causal qualification
Expressly recorded: the reviewable decision is affirmed. A further claim that affirmation caused a particular later loss is not established by the orders page.
Corroborating records
Covering letter of the same date, ART-2021-7478-McLean-and-Comcare-Decision-12-July-2023.pdf, which says the Tribunal affirmed the decision under review under s 43 of the AAT Act. Comcare determination 26 May 2021, claim 1326583/1.
Evidence classification
A for the order and the catchwords on the pages read. Propositions that depend on later paragraphs of the 21-page reasons are not established by this entry.

Inspected 11 October 2026. Opening three pages extracted of 21. SHA-256 computed.

Opens “Dear Scott treadwell.” It quotes the 27 March 2023 letter, including the DSS employment sentence and the sentence about belief in disclosable conduct, and says the PID was rejected and that none of the acknowledgement or compensation sought had happened. The Tredwell letter itself.

Limitations

  • Text was taken from the first pages of each opened PDF, up to three pages, except where a hand entry says the whole short letter was read. Longer reasons were not line-read.
  • Image-only scans produced no text. Encrypted PDFs were not decrypted. One Federal Court FOI file (docs/official-drive/2023-04-26-Federal-Court-FOI-response.pdf) could not be read because the parser required cryptography for an AES algorithm.
  • Several files in the official-drive folder open with an archive cover (“Barran Dodger Legal & Ethical Trust Fund” and an AI statement). Those openings are not treated as the agency’s letter.
  • Files of 4 bytes, including some filenames that sound like correspondence, are empty placeholders. Their contents do not exist in the file.
  • Duplicate hashes were collapsed. Near-duplicate scans with different hashes, notably the two 27 March 2023 Tredwell files, are separate entries and are cross-referenced.
  • No statement in this register is exhaustive of the repository, of Google Drive, or of any agency’s holdings.
  • Branches other than main of wezzo72/Barrandodger were listed (codex/recreate-barrandodger, new-site) and were not separately audited.
  • The further pass of 11 October 2026 opened 418 candidate PDFs and registered 270 that were not byte-identical to an existing entry. It did not open every one of the 3,650 PDFs. Text is from the opening pages only.

Questions this review leaves open

  • How the 27 March 2023 sentence about Department of Social Services employment, expressly based on information provided by the correspondent, is to be read next to the same letter’s conclusion that the officer was not satisfied the disclosure was made by a public official.
  • How that PID Act letter relates, if at all, to the AAT’s 12 July 2023 SRC Act holding. They are different decisions under different Acts.
  • The operative NCAT guardianship orders of 9 October 2025, which are in the reasons PDF but were not transcribed here.
  • The contents of the five PM&C documents released under the revised FOI decision. The release bundle was located and not text-inspected.
  • Whether image-only files, including the Commonwealth Ombudsman service-restriction PDFs, contain a restriction decision. The text layer does not say so.

Last review: 11 October 2026.
